changes: Chronogram checked: pakṣa 2, bāṇa 5, tithi 15, read right to left, gives Śaka 1552 (1630 CE); era and year kept
Purpose rewritten: 'viṣṇupūjā' was not a copying purpose. It is now the king's devotion to Viṣṇu worship as the motive for commissioning the copy

date.as_written: śake mate pakṣabāṇa titibhir lakṣate gate || dvādaśyā pauṣaśuklasya

purpose: Copy commissioned by King Jagajjyoti, who was devoted to Viṣṇu worship and found no satisfaction without the words of the Purāṇas
notes: Chronogram: pakṣa (2), bāṇa (5), tithi (15). Read right to left this gives Śaka 1552 ('titibhir' = tithibhiḥ; 'lakṣate' is probably lakṣite). Śaka 1552 is 1630 CE; Pauṣa śukla 12 falls around Dec 1630 or Jan 1631. The colophon says Śaka explicitly. The catalogue's 'VS 1652' (= c. 1595 CE) conflicts with this: the cataloguer probably misread the era or the digits. 1595 also falls before the reign of Jagajjyotirmalla of Bhaktapur (r. c. 1614–1637), while Śaka 1552 falls within it. Jagajjyoti ('jagajjyotirīśa') is taken to be Jagajjyotirmalla, but the colophon gives no -malla and names no place, so the place field is left empty. 'vyalikha cūtā' is corrupt, perhaps for 'vyalikhac chubhām' or similar; the scribe's name Vinoda is clear. Bhairavasiṃha(deva) of Tīrabhukti is the author, the Oinavāra king of Mithilā. His father Narasiṃha and elder brother Hṛdayanārāyaṇa are named only in the author's praśasti, so they are not connected with this copy.
